target_customer: Track and field coaches and meet organizers
problem: Track timing relies on costly photo finish systems or hand timing; TRAC proposed RFID timing with cellular data transmission and an app.
business_model: Hardware plus software for timing (pricing not found)

founders.name: Griffin Kelly
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. Education and co-founder details appeared only in search snippets of unopened pages, so not recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate RFID timing for track events is hard; forum comments say track needs 0.1 to 0.01 second precision that RFID may not meet.

defensibility.rationale: Established photo finish vendors already certified for track; no stated moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Photo finish vendors such as Lynx pair with chip systems; no dated 2016 response found.

market_need_then: No dated source on demand was found; the only need evidence is the YC description that TRAC aimed to simplify the track and field experience, and a 2021 forum thread arguing RFID lacks the precision track timing needs.

branding.name_origin: Name expands to Timing and Racing Around the Clock per a Wellfound profile title

outcome_analysis: TRAC was a Chicago startup in YC Winter 2016 building RFID based track timing. It is listed inactive, no funding amount beyond a Crunchbase pre-seed label was found, and no shutdown news or cause is public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: tracchicago.com failed to resolve (dead or blocked). Pre-seed round comes from the Crunchbase page label only, no amount or date. Competitor list empty: only current vendor pages found, none dated near the batch. Round Funded pages are reconstructions and were not used.
